Sentence D comes next and presents the contrast that despite the benefits these solutions may provide, they do not address the structural needs.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

If I was you, I would consider taking some time off to recharge and reflect on what's important in life.

The corrected sentence: If I were you, I would consider taking some time off to recharge and reflect on what's important in life.

questions.q_en: Describe how you will say What is Tina carrying in her bag? in passive voice.
options_en: When is being carried by Tina in her bag?
When is carried by Tina in her bag?
Why will be carried by Tina in her bag?
What is being carried by Tina in her bag?
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb 'being' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

Case 1: "Which/What" etc are placed as they are.

For example:

What are you doing? (Active)

What is being done by you? (Passive)

Case 2: When "Which/What" is used as a subject in Active voice, it is changed into "By what" in Passive voice.

For example:

What is making you happy? (Active)

By what are you being made happy? (Passive)

Also, the sentence is in the Present continuous tense in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Present continuous tense should be used.

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher will never / give you punishment / if you will / come on time.
questions.solution_en: The error is in the segment "if you will." In English, the simple present tense is used in conditional clauses introduced by "if" when referring to future possibilities, not the future tense with "will." The correct form is "if you come on time." Thus, the sentence should read: "The teacher will never give you punishment if you come on time." The other segments are correct: "the teacher will never" is a valid subject and verb phrase, "give you punishment" is acceptable (though "impose punishment" might be more formal), and "come on time" is grammatically sound.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order with the first part being fixed. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

Infants begin to smile and show excitement when

B. And display what is considered

C. Positive stimulus events are withdrawn

D. To be sadness when

E. Presented with familiar faces,
questions.solution_en:
The correct order to form a meaningful sentence is EBDC. Part E comes first as it is directly linked with the fixed (first) part. The fixed part states that the infants begin to smile and show excitement when something happens. Part E specifies the condition under which infants begin to smile and show excitement - when they are presented with familiar faces. Part B continues the sentence by introducing another reaction of the infants - displaying something that is considered to be a different emotion. Part D completes the thought started in B by specifying what the infants are displaying - sadness (Accordingly, BD forms a necessary pair). Part C completes the sentence by specifying the condition that causes the infants to display sadness - when positive stimulus events are withdrawn. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: Infants begin to smile and show excitement when presented with familiar faces, and display what is considered to be sadness when positive stimulus events are withdrawn.

Barney exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined. (Indirect Speech)

Barney said, "Good Heavens! I am ruined." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

exclaimed with sorrow thatsaid, "Good Heavens!"
heI
had donehave done

Therefore, the correct answer is: (d) The student said, "Good Heavens! I have done such a mistake."

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

Sometimes the fog is so ______ that these lights cannot be ______, but most lighthouses _______ great fog bells or fog horns; some of the latter are made to sound by steam and can be ________ for a long distance.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence talks about how lighthouses work.

In blank 1, all the adjectives are qualifying the noun 'fog' so all can fit here.

In blank 2, 'lights cannot be heard' is an illogical statement, thus, option (d) is eliminated.

In blank 3, 'lighthouses' is a plural noun so the use of the singular verb 'has' is incorrect, a plural verb will be used here, thus option (c) is eliminated.

In blank 4, 'Modal + be' is always followed by a participle form of verb so the use of the base verb 'gather' is incorrect.

'Dense, seen, have, heard' is the right set of words for the blanks.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

NOTE-

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

Most of the flowers bloom in the spring season but they start to ________ during summer.
questions.solution_en:
 Bloom means to flower or flourish, and its antonym is wither, which means to dry up or fade away.

 Flush, flourish, and blossom are all synonyms of bloom, not antonyms.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Abandon
questions.solution_en:
'Abandon' means to give up control. 'Retain' means to keep in possession or use. So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

'Relinquish' means to retire from something.

'Forsake' means to leave permanently.

'Surrender' means to give up on the power of another.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.

The farmer harvested a bountiful crop of ____ from his field.
questions.solution_en:
"Maize" is the correct homonym for this sentence. Maize is a type of cereal grain, also known as corn in some regions. It is a common crop harvested by farmers. So, the correct answer is (b) 'Maize', as it is the word that fits the context of harvesting a crop in a field.

The complete sentence is: The farmer harvested a bountiful crop of maize from his field.

The rest of the words don't fit in contextually.

Mace - a spice made from the dried shell of nutmeg/ a decorated rod that is carried by or put in front of particular public officials as a symbol of their authority.

Maze - a network of paths and hedges designed as a puzzle through which one has to find a way.

Mase - something that causes bewilderment or mystery.
